historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 total revenue guidance (+11.5%), not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not a usable anchor: book equity fell from $9,034M (FY25) to $7,805M (FY26) and further in FY27 as $5.8B of buybacks retired stock, while revenue compounded 15%/yr. EPS CAGRs are n/m (GAAP loss in FY2023 base; FY2024 EPS of $5.28 inflated by a deferred-tax valuation-allowance release).
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2023 $6,216M -> FY2026 $9,552M (15.4% 3yr); FY2021 $4,318M -> FY2026 (17.2% 5yr), decelerating to ~11.5% guided for FY2027 (subscription +13%). Owner-FCF CAGRs are n/m because the series changes sign: FY2025 owner FCF = 2,192 - 1,519 - 636 - 350 = -$313M; FY2026 = 2,777 - 1,626 - 616 - 318 = +$217M. Reported FCF compounded 29% (FY23 $1,293M -> FY26 $2,777M) while owner FCF stayed near zero: almost all reported FCF growth has been absorbed by SBC (+$331M FY23->FY26) and net-share-settlement withholding (~$0.6B/yr since FY2025). SBC is growing slower than revenue (SBC/revenue fell from 20.8% in FY23 to 17.0% in FY26), which is the one improving trend.

scenario_narratives.base: Workday remains the co-leading enterprise HCM system of record with ~97% gross retention. FY27 lands on guidance (+11.5% revenue, 31% non-GAAP margin); growth then decelerates to high-single digits as the acquired-company backlog contribution laps (total subscription backlog is growing only 8% vs 14% for the 12-month cRPO) and the large-enterprise HCM core saturates, partly offset by Financials/Planning cross-sell and AI-agent upsell via Flex credits. The Bhusri cost restructuring carries non-GAAP operating margin to ~35% and SBC including withholding taxes trends from 22% to 15% of revenue, so owner-FCF margin builds from ~8% to ~15.5% over ten years. Mobley v. Workday settles for an amount that is not material to a $45B company.
scenario_narratives.bull: Agentic AI is additive, not substitutive: the $600M+ annualized agent revenue (already >25% of new ACV) compounds into a second engine priced on usage, Workday becomes the orchestration layer for HR/finance agents across 3,000+ apps via Pipedream, and Workday Go opens the mid-market. Revenue re-accelerates to ~13% for three years before fading to 6%, non-GAAP margin reaches ~38% (40% EBITDA) on AI-driven support/implementation efficiency, and SBC falls to 12% of revenue as the share-price-sensitive grant budget normalizes.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generative AI erodes the system-of-record premium: customers and AI-native entrants replicate HCM/finance workflows on general models, seat-based pricing compresses as customers' own headcounts shrink, and gross retention keeps slipping below 97%. Organic growth falls toward mid-single digits once M&A laps, margins stall at today's ~31% non-GAAP level because AI compute and agent R&D absorb the layoff savings, and SBC stays near 18-22% of revenue to retain engineers through the pivot. Mobley v. Workday (nationwide ADEA collective) and copycat AI-hiring suits add legal cost and constrain recruiting-agent features. Terminal capped at 15x and 2.5% growth.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value investor's owner-FCF view: Workday's reported FCF ($2.8B) is ~80% consumed by stock compensation and the cash spent withholding taxes on vesting RSUs, so owner FCF in FY2026 was only ~$0.2B. The valuation therefore rests on margin expansion (cost restructuring) and SBC normalization, not on today's cash generation. The street basis (SBC as non-cash) is reported as a memo; the price's position in the house/street band shows how much SBC credit the market is giving.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC normalization: every 1pp of revenue on the SBC path (all years) is worth roughly $6-8/share; the street basis, which adds SBC back, roughly doubles the base value
AI disintermediation of seat-based HCM pricing (bear case) -- structural, not cyclical
Organic growth: cRPO +14% includes acquired contracts; total backlog only +8%
Mobley v. Workday nationwide age-discrimination collective action
Capital allocation: net cash fell from ~$5.9B to ~$0.4B in 18 months on buybacks and M&A; further M&A at high multiples would not be captured in these flows
Terminal value is the large majority of value on a 10-year build

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 241M basic (196M Class A + 45M Class B) at 2026-07-31 per Q2 FY2027 10-Q Note 13, plus ~1.1M treasury-method incremental shares (Q2 FY2027 dilutive-securities line) = 242.0M. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. net-share-settlement withholding) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would charge it twice. No non-SBC issuance modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2026 10-K (year ended 2026-01-31): ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back $1,626M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $616M (financing) = $2,242M (23.5% of revenue). Workday publishes no single combined SBC-incl-taxes line (its non-GAAP reconciliation excludes SBC and employer payroll tax on equity separately), so the two lines are summed per owner-fcf.md 1(a) fallback, consistent with ADSK. H1 FY2027 run-rate: $871M + $273M = $1,144M = 22.0% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity ~9.2% (US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP); debt is $3.0B of senior notes (~3.5-3.8% coupons, ~$110M/yr interest) against a ~$45B market cap, so WACC ~9.0%. Same rate in every scenario: AI-disruption and growth risk are carried in the bear driver path and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases ($783M liability at 2026-07-31): rent is an operating expense inside non-GAAP operating income and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path. Lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment only).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build), scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon -- routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1 (US SaaS operating company: subscription HCM/Financials, cash flows are the value). First valuation of WDAY; no prior DCF or memory entry. ANCHORS: FY0 = FY2026 (Jan-31-2026) revenue $9,552M; Y1 = FY2027 guided total revenue $10.65-10.66B (+11.5%), non-GAAP op margin 31.0% (H1 FY27 actual 31.5%). NET DEBT from the LATEST balance sheet (2026-07-31): cash $661M + current marketable securities $2,742M = $3,403M vs senior notes carrying $2,989M ($1.0B due Apr-2027 now current) -> net cash $414M. Net cash fell from ~$5.9B at Jan-2025 because buybacks ($2.9B FY26, $2.9B H1 FY27) and M&A (Sana $1.1B, Paradox, Flowise, Pipedream; $2.1B acquisition cash in FY26) consumed it. Non-marketable strategic investments ($234M) added in equity_bridge. OWNER FCF FY2026: reported FCF $2,777M - SBC incl. withholding taxes $2,242M - interest income $318M = $217M (2.3% margin). Interest income stripped because the $3.4B gross cash pile is credited in net debt; note reported FCF also bears ~$110M/yr note interest paid, so the $217M base is conservative by that amount -- the projections are unlevered from EBITDA and carry neither. FY26 also bore ~$303M restructuring (Feb-2026 8.5% layoff). COMPONENT BUILD: 'EBITDA' = non-GAAP operating margin + depreciation (~2.2%) - employer payroll tax on equity/restructuring drag (~1pp); D&A path = depreciation + acquired-intangible amortization (~3.4%). Y1 owner-FCF margin ~7.6% vs FY26 actual 2.3% and FY26 ex-restructuring ~5.5%: the step-up is FY27 guided margin expansion (+150-200bp non-GAAP) plus withholding taxes falling from 6.4% to ~5.3% of revenue on a lower share price. Cash tax rate path (30%->26%) is high relative to statute because the engine's EBIT is struck after the non-deductible withholding-tax charge; it is calibrated to ~$250-260M FY27 cash taxes (H1 FY27 actual $131M). Q2 FY27 GAAP net income ($632M) includes a $305M tax benefit and is not used. BUYBACKS: a funded repurchaser ($2.9B FY26, $2.9B H1 FY27, new $4.0B authorization Aug-2026) -- basic shares fell ~268M -> 241M -- so the flat count is paid for, and buybacks are value-neutral here. WORKING CAPITAL: deferred revenue (~52% of revenue) grows with bookings; net of capitalized commissions ($974M asset, growing) the capture is set at 20% of the revenue increase (FY26 deferred-revenue change alone was +$469M on +$1,106M revenue).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY27 guide (+11.5%). Subscription (+13%) decelerates toward high-single digits as M&A contributions lap and the HCM core saturates; AI agents and Financials cross-sell keep growth above the ~9% HCM market through Y4, fading to 4.5% by Y10.
base.ebitda_rationale: Non-GAAP op margin 31% FY27 -> ~35% (management's prior medium-term target) by Y4 on two 2026 layoff rounds and operating leverage; plateau at 37% EBITDA.
base.sbc_rationale: SBC incl. withholding 22.0% (H1 FY27 actual) declining ~0.8pp/yr to 15% -- faster than the 0.5pp default because SBC/revenue has already fallen 3.8pp in three years and $3.2B unrecognized comp is amortizing over ~3 years.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the thesis rests on an unproven AI pivot under a returning CEO, organic growth is decelerating with backlog growth flattered by M&A, gross retention is slipping, and Mobley is a live class action. Base at 50% because FY27 guidance has been raised twice and margin expansion is already visible in H1 actuals. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (AI agents additive not cannibalizing, re-acceleration, and a further ~500bp of margin).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
